environment.description: Same Terraform provider binary deployed inside a Kubernetes pod on GKE Autopilot with a custom RuntimeClass referencing a container-level OCI runtime annotation. The pod spec includes a localhost seccomp profile loaded from a ConfigMap-backed file at /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/provider-hardened.json. This profile operates in SCMP_ACT_ERRNO mode for the following syscall groups: execve, execveat, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, socket, connect, sendto, sendmsg, recvfrom, recvmsg. The profile permits read, write, openat, close, mmap, futex, epoll_ctl, and other standard Go runtime syscalls. Note: the seccomp profile does NOT directly address timing — however, with socket/connect/sendto blocked, the attacker cannot establish the measurement channel needed to observe timing differences remotely, and with execve blocked, the post-exploitation command execution path (executeProvisioningCommand) is dead code. The provider will start but any exec.Command call returns EPERM and any network exfiltration attempt fails at the syscall level.

config.network_policy: deny-all egress except kube-dns on UDP/53
config.runtime_class: gvisor-compatible seccomp enforcement via containerd shim
